skill.description: Write Playwright E2E tests using fixtures and best practices. Use when creating E2E tests, writing browser automation tests, or testing user flows.

## Query Priority (Accessibility-First)

Use queries in this order of preference:

### 1. Role Queries (Best)

```typescript
// Buttons, links, headings
await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i })
await page.getByRole('link', { name: /home/i })
await page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 })

// Form elements
await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /email/i })
await page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: /remember me/i })
await page.getByRole('combobox', { name: /country/i })

// With state
await page.getByRole('checkbox', { checked: true })
await page.getByRole('tab', { selected: true })
```

### 2. Label Queries (Forms)

```typescript
await page.getByLabel(/email address/i)
await page.getByLabel(/password/i)
await page.getByLabel(/phone number/i)
```

### 3. Text Queries (Content)

```typescript
await page.getByText(/welcome back/i)
await page.getByText('Exact Match')
```

### 4. Placeholder Queries (Fallback)

```typescript
await page.getByPlaceholder('Search...')
```

### 5. Test ID (Last Resort)

```typescript
// Only when no accessible alternative exists
await page.getByTestId('complex-widget')
```

# Write Playwright Tests

Write end-to-end tests using Playwright fixtures, Page Object Model, and role-based queries.

## Core Principles

Follow the principle of testing from the user's perspective: simulate real interactions and verify visible outcomes.

### Test User Behavior, Not Implementation

- Interact with the UI exactly as a user would
- Verify UI state, not internal logic
- Focus on flows, not isolated steps

## Query Priority (Accessibility-First)

Use queries in this order of priority:

### 1. Role Queries (Best)

```typescript
await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i })
await page.getByRole('link', { name: /home/i })
await page.getByRole('heading', { name: /welcome/i })

// Form controls
await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /email/i })
await page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: /agree/i })
await page.getByRole('combobox', { name: /country/i })
```

### 2. Label Queries (Forms)

```typescript
await page.getByLabel(/email/i)
await page.getByLabel(/password/i)
```

### 3. Text Queries (Content)

```typescript
await page.getByText(/successfully saved/i)
await page.getByText('Exact text')
```

### 4. Placeholder Queries (Fallback)

```typescript
await page.getByPlaceholder('Search...')
```

### 5. Test ID (Last Resort)

```typescript
await page.getByTestId('custom-element')
```

## Fixtures

### Why Use Fixtures?

- **Encapsulation**: Combine setup and cleanup
- **Reusability**: Use across multiple tests
- **Isolation**: Fresh state per test

### Basic Custom Fixture

```typescript
// fixtures/test-fixtures.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test'

type MyFixtures = {
  testUser: { email: string; password: string }
}

export const test = base.extend<MyFixtures>({
  testUser: async ({}, use) => {
    const user = {
      email: `user-${Date.now()}@example.com`,
      password: 'SecurePass1!',
    }
    // Setup
    await use(user)
    // Teardown (optional)
  },
})

export { expect } from '@playwright/test'
```

### Authentication Fixture

```typescript
// fixtures/auth-fixtures.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test'

type AuthFixtures = {
  authedPage: Page
}

export const test = base.extend<AuthFixtures>({
  authedPage: async ({ page }, use) => {
    await page.goto('/login')
    await page.getByLabel(/email/i).fill('admin@example.com')
    await page.getByLabel(/password/i).fill('password')
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click()
    await page.waitForURL('/dashboard')
    await use(page)
  },
})

export { expect } from '@playwright/test'
```

### Worker-Scoped Fixture

```typescript
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test'

type WorkerFixtures = {
  workerToken: string
}

export const test = base.extend<{}, WorkerFixtures>({
  workerToken: [
    async ({ browser }, use) => {
      const context = await browser.newContext()
      const page = await context.newPage()
      // … obtain token once per worker
      await context.close()
      await use('my-token')
    },
    { scope: 'worker' },
  ],
})
```

## Page Object Model

### Page Object Structure

```typescript
// pages/login.page.ts
import { type Page, type Locator } from '@playwright/test'

export class LoginPage {
  readonly page: Page
  readonly emailInput: Locator
  readonly passwordInput: Locator
  readonly submitButton: Locator
  readonly errorMessage: Locator

  constructor(page: Page) {
    this.page = page
    this.emailInput = page.getByLabel(/email/i)
    this.passwordInput = page.getByLabel(/password/i)
    this.submitButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i })
    this.errorMessage = page.getByRole('alert')
  }

  async goto() {
    await this.page.goto('/login')
  }

  async login(email: string, password: string) {
    await this.emailInput.fill(email)
    await this.passwordInput.fill(password)
    await this.submitButton.click()
  }
}
```

### Using Page Objects with Fixtures

```typescript
// fixtures/page-fixtures.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test'
import { LoginPage } from '../pages/login.page'
import { DashboardPage } from '../pages/dashboard.page'

type PageFixtures = {
  loginPage: LoginPage
  dashboardPage: DashboardPage
}

export const test = base.extend<PageFixtures>({
  loginPage: async ({ page }, use) => {
    await use(new LoginPage(page))
  },
  dashboardPage: async ({ page }, use) => {
    await use(new DashboardPage(page))
  },
})
```

## Writing Tests

### Basic Test Structure

```typescript
// tests/login.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from './fixtures'

test.describe('Login Flow', () => {
  test('user can log in with valid credentials', async ({ loginPage }) => {
    await loginPage.goto()
    await loginPage.login('user@example.com', 'correct-password')

    await expect(loginPage.page).toHaveURL('/dashboard')
    await expect(
      loginPage.page.getByRole('heading', { name: /dashboard/i })
    ).toBeVisible()
  })

  test('user sees error on invalid login', async ({ loginPage }) => {
    await loginPage.goto()
    await loginPage.login('bad@user.com', 'wrong')

    await expect(loginPage.errorMessage).toContainText(/invalid/i)
  })
})
```

### Test with Authentication Fixture

```typescript
import { test, expect } from './fixtures'

test.describe('Dashboard', () => {
  test('authenticated user can see profile', async ({ authedPage }) => {
    await authedPage.goto('/dashboard')

    await expect(
      authedPage.getByRole('heading', { name: /my account/i })
    ).toBeVisible()
  })
})
```

## Web-First Assertions

Always use auto‑waiting assertions:

```typescript
// Good – waits for element
await expect(page.getByText('Saved')).toBeVisible()

// Bad – no retry
const visible = await page.getByText('Saved').isVisible()
expect(visible).toBe(true)
```

### Common Assertions

```typescript
await expect(locator).toBeVisible()
await expect(locator).toBeHidden()
await expect(locator).toHaveText('Exact')
await expect(locator).toContainText('partial')
await expect(locator).toHaveAttribute('href', '/path')
await expect(locator).toBeEnabled()
await expect(locator).toBeDisabled()
await expect(locator).toHaveValue('value')
await expect(page).toHaveURL('/path')
await expect(page).toHaveTitle('Title')
```

## Soft Assertions

```typescript
test('multiple checks', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings')
  await expect.soft(page.getByTestId('notifications')).toContainText('On')
  await expect.soft(page.getByTestId('theme')).toContainText('Dark')
  // Continues even if soft assertions fail
})
```

## Common Patterns

### Wait for Network

```typescript
await page.goto('/dashboard')
await page.waitForResponse('/api/data')
```

### File Upload

```typescript
await page.getByLabel(/upload/i).setInputFiles('./test.pdf')
```

### Handling Dialogs

```typescript
page.on('dialog', (dialog) => dialog.dismiss())
await page.getByRole('button', { name: /delete/i }).click()
```

## What NOT to Do

- **DON'T** use `page.locator('.class')` – prefer role/label queries
- **DON'T** use `page.waitForTimeout()` – use auto‑waiting assertions
- **DON'T** test internal state – test visible behavior
- **DON'T** repeat authentication – use fixtures
- **DON'T** hardcode test data – generate unique values

## Test Organization

```
tests/
├── fixtures/
│   ├── index.ts
│   ├── auth-fixtures.ts
│   └── page-fixtures.ts
├── pages/
│   ├── login.page.ts
│   ├── dashboard.page.ts
│   └── profile.page.ts
├── auth.spec.ts
├── dashboard.spec.ts
└── profile.spec.ts
```

## Tips for Reliable Tests

1. Use unique data to avoid collisions
2. Clean up after test runs (fixture teardown)
3. Keep tests independent and focused
4. Write descriptive test names
5. Test happy and unhappy paths
